ai_summary: Great Britain currently records a total wind output of 4.9 GW, with Scottish wind generation contributing an estimated 2.1 GW, representing 20.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. While Scotland maintains an exemplary carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh, the wider GB grid stands significantly higher at 201 gCO2/kWh. Transmission bottlenecks between Scotland and southern demand centres continue to undermine this clean generation profile. Through the Balancing Mechanism, 41.7 GWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today, incurring a direct constraint cost of about £1,447,805. Because this displaced zero-carbon power must be substituted by fossil generation elsewhere, an estimated 7,919,827 m³ of natural gas has been burned in its place, releasing an avoidable 14,589 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Annualising today's expenditure reveals an estimated total yearly curtailment cost of approximately £528 million, which increases electricity invoices across the UK by an estimated £2/MWh. This stark operational divergence highlights the mounting costs of grid friction, where consumers shoulder substantial financial and environmental penalties for renewable power that is generated but cannot be transmitted.
